_about: A quest is offered by its `giver` once every quest in `requires` is done, and handed in to its `turnIn` npc once every objective is met. Objectives: kill (an enemy type, counted from when the quest is taken), collect (an item carried; taken on hand-in unless `keep`), examine (a world point), talk (go and speak to the turn-in npc; met at once). Quests sharing a `choice` are one decision: taking one locks the others. `setsFlag` records the outcome for dialogue and the world. `location` names a world.json location for the minimap. `offer`, `progress` and `complete` are what the giver says at each step. Puzzle objectives name a mechanism in the active world’s puzzles list. They require a real solved state, not an examined marker. zone groups quests in the log; level is advisory.

quests.name: The Missing Delivery
quests.summary: Mara Venn's iron never reached the old watch post. Follow the Fallen Road and find out what became of it.
quests.offer: Iron's late, and the watch post won't answer its door. Nine bars of grave-iron with my mark on them went up that road. Find out what happened and I'll pay for it.
quests.progress: Any word of my iron? A cart doesn't vanish. Look it over properly if you find it. A carter keeps papers.
quests.complete: That's Hollin's hand, and my mark on the iron. Bells at Hallow Cut. I don't like that at all. Here, as promised, and take this pack. Keep a torch and a rod loose in your kit and you'll lose both. If you mean to look further, look north, into the Blackwood. That's where the carters turn off.
quests.turnInLog: You hand Mara the manifest. She reads it twice.

quests.name: Bells at Hallow Cut
quests.summary: Hollin's manifest warns of bells at Hallow Cut, the old burial ground east of the road. Look over the graves and put down whatever walks there.
quests.offer: Graves don't ring. I've buried enough folk to know. Something's walking at Hallow Cut, and big, by the tracks on the road. Go and look at the graves, and if whatever rings those bells can be put down, put it down.
quests.progress: Still ringing? Then it's still walking.
quests.complete: A brute in grave-chains, carrying a watchman's blade? Then the watch post didn't just stop answering. Someone emptied it. Take this. You've earned it.

objectives.label: Look over the graves at Hallow Cut

quests.name: The Wolf Den
quests.summary: The carters turned north into the Blackwood, past a den of barrow wolves beside the track. Thin the pack and search the den for any sign of them.
quests.offer: The carters turned north into the Blackwood. They'd not have got far. There's a den of barrow wolves by the track, past the shrine at the forest edge. Thin the pack, and tell me if you see any sign of my carters.
quests.progress: The wolves hunt in threes. Don't let them get round you.
quests.complete: No carters, then. Only bones and a purse. I'd hoped otherwise. The track's safer for it, at least. Take these. You'll want them deeper in.

quests.name: The Seer in the Glade
quests.summary: Someone is calling the dead up out of the Blackwood. Hunters speak of a seer among the standing stones in the far glade, and of archers camped on the way. Go deep and end it.
quests.offer: Bells under the Cut, a brute in a watchman's gear, wolves fat on carters. Someone is calling the dead up out of the Blackwood. The hunters talk of a seer among the standing stones in the far glade, and archers camped on the way. Go deep, Warden. End it.
quests.progress: The glade is at the end of the track. You'll know the stones.
quests.complete: It's quieter. I felt it at the anvil before you came up the track. Here, the best shield I've made this year. Keep it between you and whatever comes next.

objectives.label: Find the standing stones in the glade

quests.name: Perch for the Pot
quests.summary: Hester Vale at the Ford Inn wants fresh perch from the mere for her kitchen. Catch three and bring them to her.
quests.offer: WANTED: three good perch, fresh, for the inn's kitchen. Fair coin paid. Ask for Hester at the Ford Inn. (Not eels. Never again eels.)
quests.progress: No perch yet? Tam will show you which end of the rod goes in the water.
quests.complete: Now those are perch. The stew will taste of something tonight. Here, for your trouble.

quests.name: Meat for Winter
quests.summary: The town is short of meat for the winter stores. Bring four cuts of wolf meat to Hester at the Ford Inn.
quests.offer: The cellar's half empty and the frost is coming. Meat wanted, any honest kind. The barrow wolves in the woods are lean, but they'll salt. Bring it to the Ford Inn. H. Vale.
quests.progress: The salt barrel's still waiting.
quests.complete: That'll keep a family through a bad week. Thank you. Truly.

quests.name: Pelts for the Boat
quests.summary: Old Tam wants wolf pelts to stuff the seams of his boat. Bring him two. Wolves have to be skinned for their pelts: Agna Holt, the tanner in Brackenford, teaches Skinning.
quests.offer: Boat leaks. Need two pelts to caulk her, wolf will do. Bring them to the mere. Tam.
quests.progress: Still leaking, she is.
quests.complete: Good thick hides. She'll float another year. Take this, and mind the edge.

quests.name: Clear the Road
quests.summary: The dead walk the Fallen Road north of town. Put down four Ashen Ghouls and tell Mara Venn at her forge it is done.
quests.offer: BY ORDER OF THE TOWN: the road north is unsafe. Any able hand who puts down the walking dead on the Fallen Road will be paid at the forge. Mara Venn will settle.
quests.progress: The road's no quieter yet.
quests.complete: Four of them? The carters will thank you, even if they never learn your name. Here's the town's coin.

quests.name: Bounty: Old Greyjaw
quests.summary: A huge grey wolf, Old Greyjaw, roams the Blackwood and has killed two trappers. Put it down and claim the bounty from Mara Venn at her forge.
quests.offer: BOUNTY. A grey wolf the size of a pony roams the Blackwood. It has taken two trappers and a mule. Whoever kills OLD GREYJAW will be paid at the forge. Do not go alone. (You will go alone.)
quests.progress: Greyjaw's still out there. You'd hear the howling stop.
quests.complete: That's Greyjaw's blood on you? Then the trappers can go back in. The bounty's yours, and well earned.

quests.name: Carp for Sunday
quests.summary: Hester wants two bramble carp from the Stillwater Mere for the Sunday table.
quests.offer: Sunday's the one day folk here eat like they mean it. Carp hide under the reeds at the mere. Bring me two and I'll show you how to bake them.
quests.progress: No carp? Try the reeds. Patience, mostly.
quests.complete: Look at the size of them. Here, that's how you bake a carp, and a couple to see you on your way.

quests.name: Supper at the Ford
quests.summary: The inn is full and Hester's short of hands. Cook three grilled perch and two roast dace and bring them to her.
quests.offer: Carters in, and every one of them hungry. I can't be at the hearth and the tap at once. Cook me three grilled perch and two roast dace, would you?
quests.progress: They're banging their mugs out there.
quests.complete: Not burnt, not raw. You've the knack. Here's your share of the night's takings.

quests.name: The Ghost in the Mere
quests.summary: Hester's mother made a broth from a pale fish called the ghostfin. Catch one in the Stillwater Mere and bring it to her. It is very rare.
quests.offer: My mother made a broth from ghostfin. One bowl and you'd walk through snow. I haven't tasted it in twenty years. Tam says they still bite, once in a blue moon. Catch me one?
quests.progress: Still fishing? Tam says it took him a whole winter.
quests.complete: Oh. Oh, that's one. I'll write the broth down for you, it's only fair. And take this, it was my mother's.

quests.name: Wood for the Hearth
quests.summary: Hester needs five bundles of firewood from the deadfall in the Blackwood to keep the inn's fire lit.
quests.offer: The woodpile's down to splinters and the nights are drawing in. There's deadfall all through the Blackwood. Bring me five bundles and the fire stays lit.
quests.progress: Still cold in here, love. The deadfall's north, past the watch post.
quests.complete: That'll see us through the week. Warm yourself before you go.

quests.name: Ore for the Forge
quests.summary: Mara wants four lumps of bog-iron ore from the rocks in Hallow Cut.
quests.offer: Grave-iron won't last forever. There's bog-iron in the rocks at Hallow Cut, red as rust. Bring me four lumps and I'll have something to work with.
quests.progress: The red stone, in the Cut. Hit it until it gives.
quests.complete: Good weight to these. I'll get them in the furnace tonight.

quests.name: Sorrel from the Mere
quests.summary: Tam wants six sprigs of mere sorrel from the wet ground around the Stillwater Mere.
quests.offer: Mere sorrel. Sharp green stuff, grows round the edge of the Stillwater and nowhere else. Fish taste of nothing without it. Six sprigs, if you're passing.
quests.progress: Round the water's edge. Smell it before you see it.
quests.complete: That's the stuff. Here, for your trouble.

quests.name: First Hides
quests.summary: Agna Holt the tanner wants five boar hides, skinned clean, to see whether you have the hands for it.
quests.offer: Everyone who comes through that gate thinks they can skin. Most of them bring me something that looks like it lost an argument with a plough. Bring me five boar hides, whole, from the boar east of the road. If they're fit to tan, I'll give you a better knife than the one you're holding.
quests.progress: Five hides. Whole. Not in ribbons.
quests.complete: Hm. Not bad. Not good, but not bad. Here. My second-best knife. Look after it better than you looked after these.

quests.name: Pelts from the Ridge
quests.summary: Agna Holt wants four ridge wolf pelts. The wolves hunt the high ground east of the road, south of Hallow Cut. They are level 4, so you need Skinning 10 to skin them.
quests.offer: Winter's coming and everyone in Brackenford suddenly remembers they own no warm coat. Wolf pelt. Four of them, from the ridge east of the road. The wolves run in packs, so don't go up there whistling. And you'll want ten in the skill before they come off clean.
quests.progress: Four pelts. The ridge, east of the road.
quests.complete: Good thick fur. Someone in this town will be warm because of you, and they'll never once think to thank you. That's tanning.

quests.name: Boar for the Spit
quests.summary: Hester at the Ford Inn wants five boar haunches for the spit. Wild boar root about the fields east of the road and round the farms.
quests.offer: BOAR WANTED for the spit. Five haunches, fresh, and I'll pay fair coin. The boar east of the road are fat on everybody's turnips. H. Vale, the Ford Inn.
quests.progress: The spit's turning with nothing on it.
quests.complete: Now that's a smell to bring folk in out of the rain. Here, and I'll show you the spit if you've the coin.

quests.name: Bounty: Old Bristleback
quests.summary: Old Bristleback, a boar the size of a cart, has broken every fence on the Fallen Road. Kill it and claim Bram Corrick's bounty at his farm.
quests.offer: BOUNTY. OLD BRISTLEBACK, the great boar, has broke my fences nine times this year and gored my good dog. Kill it and bring word to Corrick farm. B. Corrick. (Underneath, in another hand: and good riddance to you both.)
quests.progress: Still out there. I can hear my fences going.
quests.complete: Dead? Truly? Thirty years that pig's been laughing at me. Here, take it, every coin. I'd give you the dog too, if he'd go.

quests.name: Black Barley
quests.summary: Edda Ashby's barley is rotting in the ground and she is sure the Corricks have poisoned it. Look at the field and the boundary stone on the hedge, then tell her what you saw.
quests.offer: Look at it. Look at my barley. Thirty years my family's farmed this ground and it's never once come up black. Then the Corricks start sniffing round the hedge, and now this. Salt, or worse. Go and look at the field, and the stone on the hedge while you're at it. Then come and tell me I'm wrong. You won't.
quests.progress: Well? Did you look, or did you just stand there?
quests.complete: Lifted turf at the stone. Someone careful, you say. Oh, Bram Corrick's careful. Careful as a fox in a henhouse.

quests.name: Over the Hedge
quests.summary: Edda wants Bram Corrick told, to his face, that she knows what he has done. He farms the land south of the hedge.
quests.offer: I'll not set foot on Corrick land. My mother never did and her mother never did. But you can. Go and tell Bram Corrick I know what he's done to my field, and that the reeve will hear of it.
quests.progress: Corrick. South of the hedge. Follow the smell.
quests.complete: Poisoned her barley? Me? I've not been over that hedge since her husband's burying, and I only went then to make sure. You tell Edda Ashby she can bring the reeve, and he can count the boar in my fields while he's here.

quests.name: Tusks in the Turnips
quests.summary: Wild boar are tearing up the Corrick fields as well as everyone else's. Kill six, and Bram Corrick may have more to say about the Ashbys.
quests.offer: You want to talk about ruined fields? Look east. Wild boar, a sounder of them, rooting up everything I plant and half the road besides. Kill six of the brutes and I'll tell you something about that stone Edda's so worried about.
quests.progress: Still hear them grunting. Still not dead, then.
quests.complete: That's six fewer mouths. All right. About the stone. I've seen someone at it, late, more than once. Not me. And there's another thing. Three of my pigs gone from the sty since harvest, and I blamed the boar. Boar don't lift gate latches. And my hired lad, Cal. Never in his bed when I look in, and always mud on his boots from the north side. Ask him where he goes. He'll lie to me. He might not lie to you.

quests.name: A Letter Under the Stone
quests.summary: Cal Fenner, Bram Corrick's hired hand, and Wren Ashby, Edda's daughter, have been leaving each other letters under the boundary stone. With both farms watching it now, Cal wants you to take his last letter to Wren before anyone else finds it.
quests.offer: Bram's sent you, hasn't he. Look. It's me at the stone. Me and Wren Ashby. We leave letters under it, have done since harvest. A hired hand with no land and Edda Ashby's only daughter. You can see why we keep it under a stone. Nobody poisoned anybody, we just lift the turf. But Edda's watching the hedge now, and there's a letter under there with my name all over it. Get it out before her mother does. Give it to Wren. Only Wren.
quests.progress: Under the stone. Quick, before someone looks.
quests.complete: Cal sent you? Give it here. ...Oh, the fool, he's signed it. He always signs it. Thank you. Don't look at me like that. Mother would sooner see me wed a boar than a hired man off Corrick land.

objectives.label: Cal's letter, from under the stone

quests.name: What Lies Under
quests.summary: Wren Ashby says the barley started dying where the old drain comes out of the bank. Look at the drain mouth on the Ashby side of the hedge, pull three of the black nails out of it (at either end), and look for whatever else is in there.
quests.offer: It isn't the Corricks. I've told her and told her. The barley started dying by the old drain, where it comes out of the bank on our side of the hedge. It runs all the way back under Corrick land to the graves on the hill. Mother won't go near it. Look at it for me. Both ends. Whatever's in the water, bring some back. She'll need to see it.
quests.progress: The drain, by the hedge. And the far end, up by the graves, if you can stomach it.
quests.complete: Coffin nails. Somebody dug up the old graves and pushed these into our drain. On purpose. ...And this. A black rag, knotted three times. The Blackhedge lot wear those, the ones who rob the carts on the road. Why would bandits want our barley dead? ...I've seen one like it before. Hanging on the hook behind Cal's door. He said he found it on the road. Keep the nails. Somebody has to tell Mother, and she'll want proof in her hand. But ask Cal about that rag first. I can't.

objectives.label: Whatever was caught on the drain stones by the graves

quests.name: The Whole Truth
quests.summary: Tell Edda Ashby everything: the bandits, the coffin nails in the old drain, Cal's night work for them and why he did it, and Wren and Cal and their letters under the stone. Show her the nails.
quests.offer: Tell her all of it. The bandits, the drain, the nails. What Cal did, and why. And me and Cal. I'm sick of lifting turf in the dark. If she throws me out, she throws me out. At least the barley will grow.
quests.progress: Mother's in the yard. She's always in the yard.
quests.complete: Coffin nails. Bandits, in my own ground. And I spent the summer cursing Bram Corrick. ...And my Wren, with Bram's hired boy. Under my nose, all harvest. Give me a moment. No. Give me a lifetime. ...Tell Bram Corrick I'm sorry. Then tell him we're digging a new drain, together. And that boy. Hauling grave-nails into my barley for a shilling a night, to buy my daughter a ring. Of all the stupid, stupid... Tell him he can come to supper. He can dig the drain first. Then never repeat that I said any of it.
quests.turnInLog: The Ashbys and the Corricks will dig the new drain together. Wren and Cal no longer need the stone.

quests.name: Only the Drain
quests.summary: Tell Edda Ashby about the bandits and the coffin nails in the old drain, and nothing about Wren and Cal, or Cal's part in it. Show her the nails.
quests.offer: Tell her about the bandits and the drain. Only that. Not about me and Cal, and not what he did. Not yet. She's lost the barley and Father in the same few years; she'll not lose me to a hired hand on the same day. Let us keep our stone a while longer. Please.
quests.progress: Mother's in the yard. Only the drain, mind.
quests.complete: Coffin nails. Bandits, in my own ground, all this time. ...So it wasn't Corrick. I'll have the drain stopped and the bank dug out. I'll not apologise to him, mind. He'll have done something, some time. He always has.
quests.turnInLog: The old drain will be stopped. The feud cools, but the hedge stays, and so does the secret under the stone.

quests.name: Corrick's Doing
quests.summary: Edda Ashby wants a culprit, and the old drain runs under Corrick land. Give her the coffin nails and tell her the Corricks put them there. Say nothing about bandits.
quests.offer: You've been poking round that drain. I've seen you. It runs under Corrick land, every yard of it. Whatever's in it, he put there. I don't want to hear about bandits or bogles. Bring me what you found and say his name, and you'll be paid better than the Corricks could ever pay you.
quests.progress: Bring me what you found. And say his name.
quests.complete: Coffin nails. Corrick put coffin nails in my water. I knew it. I always knew it. ...Get off my land now. I've a reeve to fetch and a lantern to light, and you'll not want to be here for either.
quests.turnInLog: That night the Corrick hayrick burns. By morning Wren Ashby and Cal Fenner are gone, together, and nobody knows where.

quests.name: The Black Rag
quests.summary: Show Reeve Aldous Pell the knotted black rag from the Ashby drain.
quests.offer: You've the look of someone with something to show me, and the look of someone who'd rather not. Out with it.
quests.progress: Well? Let's see it.
quests.complete: Knotted three times. That's Blackhedge. A dozen cutthroats camped in the trees west of the forest track, past the deadfall. They rob carts and anyone poorer than themselves, and lately pigs off Corrick land, I hear. Never bothered with poisoning fields. Never had the wit to. ...Somebody's paying them.

quests.name: Eyes on Blackhedge
quests.summary: Get close enough to the Blackhedge camp, west of the forest track, to count the bandits, and no closer. Watch from the lookout rock. They are far stronger than you for now (level 6, and their captain level 8).
quests.offer: I've two watchmen, and one of them's asleep. I'll not send them up there to die. You, though. Go and look. There's a rock east of the camp you can lie behind. Count them, see who's in charge, and come back. Don't be brave. Brave is how the last fellow ended up in the ditch.
quests.progress: Count them. Don't fight them.
quests.complete: Six, and a big man in a red coat. Harl Voss. I knew Harl when he was stealing apples. He couldn't plan a picnic. Someone's planning for him.

objectives.label: Watch the camp from the lookout rock

quests.name: Thinning the Hedge
quests.summary: Thin out the Blackhedge camp: kill four cutthroats and two bowmen. They are level 6; come back stronger if you must.
quests.offer: When you're ready, and not before, I want that camp thinner. Four of the knife men, two of the bows. I'll pay from the town purse. If they're too much for you yet, there's no shame in it. There's only shame in dying in a ditch over it.
quests.progress: Still six of them laughing in the trees, last I heard.
quests.complete: That'll be talked about at the Ford tonight. Small men, Blackhedge, for all their knives. But small men with a paymaster are worth a closer look.

quests.name: Harl Voss
quests.summary: Kill Harl Voss, the Blackhedge captain (level 8, elite), and search his strongbox for whoever paid him.
quests.offer: Harl Voss. Put him down, and go through his things. Men like Harl keep everything, because they can't read well enough to know what's worth burning. I want to know who paid him to sour Edda Ashby's ground.
quests.progress: Harl's still breathing, and still being paid by someone.
quests.complete: 'Sour the ground, set the two houses at each other, and the land will come cheap.' ...Grey wax. A closed eye. I've been reeve here twenty years and I've never seen that seal. Harl was hired, and whoever hired him isn't from Brackenford, and isn't finished. I don't like that I don't know who they are. Keep your eyes open on the road.
quests.turnInLog: Somebody hired the Blackhedge bandits to ruin the Ashby farm. Their letters are sealed in grey wax, pressed with a closed eye.

quests.name: A Shilling a Night
quests.summary: Wren Ashby has seen a knotted black rag like the one from the drain hanging behind Cal Fenner's door. Ask Cal about it.
quests.offer: That rag. There's one like it on the hook behind Cal's door, I'd swear to it. He's had money lately, too, and he never has money. Go and ask him. I can't. If he lies to me I'll know, and then I'll have to know.
quests.progress: Cal. At the Corrick farm. Please.
quests.complete: ...Where did you get that? Oh, no. No, no. A man with one of those on his arm stopped me on the road at harvest. Said the Ashbys had hired him to clear their old drain and wanted it done quiet, so Edda's pride wouldn't take a knock. A shilling a night to carry sacks up from the graves and lift the capstones. Heavy sacks. I never looked inside. I was saving. For a ring. For Wren. ...I put those nails in her barley, didn't I. I did it to marry her and I've ruined her.

objectives.label: Ask Cal Fenner about the black rag

quests.name: Boar Don't Lift Latches
quests.summary: Bram Corrick's pigs have been going missing, and Reeve Pell says the Blackhedge bandits take pigs. Find out whether Bram's pigs are at the bandit camp west of the forest track, without starting a fight you can't finish.
quests.offer: Pell says it's that Blackhedge rabble taking my pigs. I'd like to know before I go up there with a pitchfork and get myself killed. Go and look. Every Corrick pig has a notch cut in its left ear, my father's mark. If they're there, I'll know. Don't get stuck for a pig, mind. Not even a good one.
quests.progress: Notch in the left ear. You can't miss it.
quests.complete: Penned up behind their fire like they own them. My pigs. ...I'll not get them back from that lot with a pitchfork. But once that camp's cleared, I'm fetching them home, and I'll not be asking nicely.

objectives.label: Find Bram's pigs at the Blackhedge camp

quests.name: Rats in the Grain
quests.summary: Rats are at the Ashby granary, the Corrick sties and the old drain between the farms. Kill eight Granary Rats for Edda Ashby.
quests.offer: Rats. In the granary, in the feed, in my boots of a morning. More than any year I can remember, and fat with it. Kill eight of the things and I'll pay you in coin, not in turnips.
quests.progress: Still hear them in the thatch at night.
quests.complete: Eight. Thank you. You know what's odd? They all come up the same way, out of the old drain by the hedge. Never used to. Something's changed down there.

quests.name: Nets on the Mere
quests.summary: Blackhedge poachers are netting Stillwater Mere bare. Drive them off: kill three Poachers and two Netmen, then report to Reeve Pell.
quests.offer: NOTICE: poachers are stripping Stillwater Mere of fish and fowl, and the Mere folk have been threatened at knifepoint. Any who drive them off will be paid by the Reeve, Aldous Pell.
quests.progress: The Mere's still being emptied. I can smell the smokehouse from here.
quests.complete: Blackhedge again, netting fish they can't eat in a season. Someone is buying it all, salted and barrelled. And paying in new coin, freshly struck. Small men don't have new coin. Keep that in mind.

quests.name: Prowlers in the Pines
quests.summary: Grey prowlers run in packs through the Blackwood and have started taking the woodcutters' dogs. Kill ten Blackwood Prowlers and report to Reeve Pell.
quests.offer: BOUNTY: ten silver-weight in coin for any who thin the prowler packs in the Blackwood. They hunt in fours. Do not go alone unless you are certain of yourself.
quests.progress: The woodcutters won't go past the deadfall yet.
quests.complete: Ten? You'll be smelling of wet dog for a week. The woodcutters say they're running from something deeper in, not hunting. I don't like that either.

quests.name: The Ogre in the Deadfall
quests.summary: An ogre has made its lair in the deadfall by the forest track, rolling logs onto carts. Put it down and report to Reeve Pell.
quests.offer: WANTED, DEAD: the ogre at the deadfall on the forest track. It has smashed two carts and a woodcutter's leg. It is large and slow. Do not stand in front of it.
quests.progress: Still squatting in the deadfall, they say, picking its teeth with a fence post.
quests.complete: Dead? Well. I'll have the carters toast you, though most of them will claim they softened it up for you.

quests.name: The Blackpool Tench
quests.summary: Old Tam wants three tench from the Blackpool, deep in the Blackwood, to know the water there is still alive. Bring them and he'll teach you the Apprentice's craft.
quests.offer: You've got the wrist for it now. Time you fished somewhere that fights back. There's a pool in the Blackwood, black as a boot. My brother fished it every spring till the wood went bad. Bring me three tench out of it. If they're fat, the water's still good. If they're thin, or they taste of iron like he used to say... well. Then I'll want to know that too.
quests.progress: Three tench from the Blackpool. Mind the trees. They watch.
quests.complete: Fat as butter. Good. Good. And the iron? No? Hm. Sit down, then. Let's talk about how a real angler holds a rod.

quests.name: Root and Blood
quests.summary: Briony wants five bloodroot from the Blackwood floor before she'll teach you the Apprentice's craft.
quests.offer: Ditchbell's a child's herb. If you want to learn, you go where the good roots are, and the good roots are where nobody sane goes. Bloodroot. Five of them, from the Blackwood. Cut them clean, don't pull. And if something follows you home, don't bring it in here.
quests.progress: Five bloodroot. Cut, not pulled.
quests.complete: Clean cuts, every one. You've the hands for it. Sit, and I'll show you what an Apprentice knows.

quests.name: The Mill Fever
quests.summary: The fever is back at the Brackenford mill. Briony needs three fortifying tonics, brewed by your own hand, before she'll teach you the Apprentice's craft.
quests.offer: It's back. The mill fever. Same as last winter: the shakes, then the sleep. I can't brew fast enough on my own. Three fortifying tonics, your own work, and we'll see if you're ready for more. And ask yourself, while you brew, why only the mill. They draw their water from the stream off the Blackwood. I've been asking myself for a year.
quests.progress: Three fortifying tonics. Your own brewing.
quests.complete: Good colour. Good smell. These'll hold the fever off a week. You've earned the Apprentice's craft. And keep your eyes open in the Blackwood. Something in that water isn't right.

quests.name: Where the Lanterns Went Out
quests.summary: Inspect the fallen lantern on the north road and put three road revenants to rest. Return to Captain Rowan at the Thornford watch house.
quests.offer: My patrol signed out at dusk. Their relief found men who had been buried for twenty years, carrying winter-work chits. Follow Lantern Road to the fallen cart. Read what is caught in the lantern, and put three revenants down before another traveller joins them. I would rather be wrong about all of this.
quests.progress: The broken lantern is beside the cart on the north road. Three revenants, then bring me what you can read. Keep clear of the deeper graveyard for now.
quests.complete: A stamped chit reads ROOK & SONS — CONTINUANCE OF SERVICE. Rowan’s jaw tightens. “Their winter grain came with a labour clause. Before we follow that seal to Old Watch, find Dunn by the fallen lantern. Paige was carrying letters through there. Bring her and the post home if you can.”
quests.chapter: The watch that never came home

quests.name: The Way Through Briarwood
quests.summary: Clear three Briarwood wolves and survey Wolf Hollow. The woodland path loops back to the watch road. This woodland errand is optional.
quests.offer: Those wolves have learned that a lunch bundle usually comes with a slow woodcutter. Clear three from Wolf Hollow and check the loop’s south end. We need one woodland route people can use without making their children heirs. This is my job, not a condition on Rowan’s.
quests.progress: Three Briarwood wolves and a survey of Wolf Hollow, south of my camp. Then come back to me here.
quests.complete: Fen checks your marks. “Good. I can send the cutters round that way. They will complain it is uphill. That is how I shall know they got home.” He hands over a tool pack.

quests.name: The Silent Watch
quests.summary: Search Old Watch, defeat the Bellkeeper and read the old charter at Dawnstone. Report to Rowan. Briarwood is an optional route.
quests.offer: The Bellkeeper used to close the working day. Now his seal is on orders calling the dead to another shift. Search Old Watch, stop him, then read the charter stone at Dawnstone. Before Rook’s people arrived, that bell meant something. We need to know what they changed.
quests.progress: Old Watch is north of the fallen cart. Dawnstone is on the path beyond it. Stop the Bellkeeper and read both places before you come back.
quests.complete: “A day’s service ends at dusk. The dead owe no labour.” Rowan reads the old words twice. “Somebody replaced a limit with a loophole.” He offers the watch’s reward. “Take this account to Morrow Finch in Mourning Hollow, east of Old Watch. He keeps the parish sick lists. He will know whose names these were.”
quests.chapter: The watch that never came home

quests.name: Something for the Road
quests.summary: Gather three ditchbell flowers beside the Briarwood path and bring them to Elsie at the Lantern Inn.
quests.offer: Blue ditchbell grows along the western woodland path. Bring me three sprigs. You need no training to pick those marked patches, and I will brew something useful for your pack.
quests.progress: Three ditchbell from the marked patches along Briarwood’s path. Bring them to Elsie inside the Lantern Inn.
quests.complete: “Three ditchbell. Very good. A little for the draughts, none for the stew.” Elsie catches your expression. “I have separate spoons. I run an inn, not a lottery.”

quests.name: Stretch Your Legs
quests.summary: Bram's cart has thrown a wheel on the west road. Walk to the milestone up the road, read it, and come back to him.
quests.offer: “Awake at last. You slept through the wheel coming off, which I count as a talent.” Bram Wenlock kicks the cart. “You rode the last forty miles on my grain sacks for nothing, so you can do me a turn. Walk up the road to the milestone and tell me how far we are from Thornford. My knees have opinions about walking.”
quests.progress: Walk with W, A, S and D (or the left stick); the road runs east. Press F beside the milestone to read it, then come back to Bram. Space hops over small things.
quests.complete: “One mile? Hah. It said one mile when I was a lad, too. Somebody keeps moving it closer to save face.” He spits, thoughtfully. “Good legs, anyway. Better than mine.”

objectives.label: Read the milestone up the road

quests.name: Rats in the Grain
quests.summary: Rats have found the sacks that spilled when Bram's wheel came off. Drive off four of them in the grass south of the road.
quests.offer: “Now the wheel is off, the rats are on. Listen to them. That is my grain they are chewing, and Elsie at the Lantern Inn has paid for half of it.” He hands you nothing at all. “You have hands and a weapon of sorts. Four of them, and the rest will get the hint.”
quests.progress: Left click a rat to choose it as your target (Tab cycles targets). Press 1, or right click it, to attack. Rats will not come to you; you go to them. If you get hurt, rest, or eat Trail Bread from your utility bar.
quests.complete: “That is the noise I like. No noise.” Bram knots a split sack shut. “You fight like someone who has never been taught. Thornford has people who teach that, if you can pay them. You cannot. Yet.”

quests.name: The Road In
quests.summary: Take Bram's note to Elsie Reed at the Lantern Inn in Thornford. On the way, look at the dark lantern post by Miller's Pool.
quests.offer: “I will be here till somebody with a spare wheel takes pity. Take this to Elsie Reed at the Lantern Inn, so she knows her grain is late and not stolen.” He looks east along the road. “And look at the lantern post by Miller's Pool as you pass. It was lit every night of my life. Last three times I came through, dark. Nobody in Thornford will say why.”
quests.progress: Follow the road east and down the hill to Miller's Pool. Look at the dark lantern post beside the road (and mind the fox that sleeps under it), then go on into Thornford. The Lantern Inn is on the west side of the square.
quests.complete: Elsie reads Bram's note twice, then folds it very small. “Late. Of course he is late. That man would be late to his own wake and then complain about the ale.” She looks you over. “He says you sorted his rats and did not steal anything. In this valley that is a reference.”
quests.turnInLog: You have reached Thornford. Elsie Reed runs the Lantern Inn; the village has work for anyone willing to do it.

objectives.label: Look at the dark lantern post
Chase off the fox under the post
Give Bram's note to Elsie at the Lantern Inn

quests.name: Odd Jobs
quests.summary: Take the Lantern Inn's broken hinge to Iren Holt at the forge across the square.
quests.offer: You have the look of someone whose purse is mostly hope. I know it well; half my regulars wear it. Here. This hinge broke on the back door last night. Take it to Iren at the forge. She owes me for a winter of soup, and she will pretend she does not. Tell her I said so, and tell her I said it kindly.
quests.progress: Iren's forge is across the square. Give her the hinge and Elsie's kind words. Mostly the hinge.
quests.complete: Iren turns the hinge over. “Soup. She means the soup.” She sighs and tosses it on the mend pile, then looks at you properly. “You have nothing to hang a tool on, have you? Here. Offcuts. It is a belt now. Rods, knives, a pick if you ever earn one. Keep them on that and your bags stay for the things you are going to lose.”
quests.turnInLog: Iren hands you a plain leather belt. Your tools have somewhere to live now. Press T to open your tool belt.

objectives.label: Bring the hinge to Iren at the forge

quests.name: Hungry Work
quests.summary: Elsie says her cook, Hobb Marrow, needs a pair of hands. Speak to him by the hearth inside the Lantern Inn.
quests.offer: Iren gave you a belt? She must like you. Do not tell her I noticed. Now, I cannot feed you for nothing; the stew would hear about it. But Hobb is short a pair of hands in the kitchen and you have two. Go and see him by the hearth. He is the one swearing at the pot.
quests.progress: Hobb Marrow cooks at the hearth inside the Lantern Inn. Follow the swearing.
quests.complete: Hobb does not look up from the pot. “Elsie sent you. Elsie sends me everyone. Last week it was a goat.” He tastes the spoon and makes a face. “No coin? No food either, then, unless you work. Right. I can use you.”

objectives.label: Speak to Hobb Marrow by the inn's hearth

quests.name: A Meal Earned
quests.summary: Bring Hobb three bundles of firewood from Osric's woodpile, two boar haunches from the young boars in Holt Meadow and three handfuls of wild garlic from under Heda's orchard hedge.
quests.offer: Here is the bargain. I have a pot and a fire and no fuel, no meat and nothing to make it taste of anything. Osric the woodcutter leaves split wood by his stump; take three bundles, he will not miss them, he will only mention it. Two boar haunches from the meadow: Heda's young boars are eating her orchard, so we are eating them. And wild garlic, three handfuls, under her hedge. Bring the lot and you eat tonight.
quests.progress: Three bundles of firewood from Osric's woodpile, two boar haunches from Holt Meadow and three handfuls of wild garlic from Heda's orchard hedge. Then back to Hobb.
quests.complete: Hobb builds the fire high, sears the boar and throws in the garlic, and the inn smells like somewhere people stay. He hands you a plate. “Eat. Then watch.” He shows you how to turn the meat on the spit so the fat bastes it. “There. Now you can feed yourself. Do not tell Elsie I teach for free, or she will charge me for it.”
quests.turnInLog: Hobb teaches you Cooking and his spit-roast boar. Any hearth or campfire will do; boar haunches come from boars.

objectives.label: Wild garlic from Heda's orchard hedge

quests.name: The Borrowed Rod
quests.summary: Tobin lends you his old rod and shows you how to cast. Catch a Gloomwater perch in Willow Pond and bring it to him.
quests.offer: Hobb sent you? Then you can cook a fish and cannot catch one. That is the wrong way round, but it is a start. Take my old rod. Do not lose it, it was my father's and he did not lose it either. Cast where the water is still, wait for the bob to dip, and strike. Bring me a perch and we will see if you have the patience.
quests.progress: Use the old rod from your tool belt at Willow Pond. When the bob dips, strike. One Gloomwater perch for Tobin.
quests.complete: Tobin weighs the perch in his hand and nods as if it has told him something. Then he holds out his other hand for the rod. “It goes home with me. Buy your own; I sell them, by coincidence.” He scribbles on a scrap. “And take this to the fire: perch fried in its own fat with Hobb's garlic. My mother's. She caught better fish than me and never let me forget it.”
quests.turnInLog: You hand back Tobin's old rod. Buy a fishing rod from him to fish again; his pan-perch recipe is in your Cooking book.

quests.name: Ore for the Forge
quests.summary: Iren lends you her spare mining pick. Bring her two lumps of tin ore from the pale outcrops east of Holt Meadow.
quests.offer: That belt looks lonely. Here, my spare pick; it has a chip in it and a temper, like its owner. There is tin in the pale rock out east, past Heda's meadow where Agna keeps her drying racks. Bring me two lumps and I will show you what the stuff is for. Then give the pick back. I know how many I own.
quests.progress: Two lumps of tin ore from the pale outcrops east of Holt Meadow, near Agna's racks. Then back to Iren's forge with her pick.
quests.complete: Iren cracks one lump on the anvil and shows you the grey glint inside. “That is tin. Copper and tin make bronze, and bronze makes everything a village needs to stay a village.” She takes her pick back. “Mining is yours now. I sell picks. You will notice I mention that last.”
quests.turnInLog: Iren teaches you Mining and takes back her spare pick. She sells mining picks at the forge.

objectives.label: Tin ore from the eastern outcrops

quests.name: Hides for Agna
quests.summary: Agna the tanner lends you a skinning knife. Skin two wild boars near her racks and bring her the hides.
quests.offer: You have hands and you have not fainted yet. That puts you ahead of the last three. Take this knife. Kill a wild boar, loot it, then work the hide off before the crows do. Two hides. Bring them and the knife back, and I will tell you whether you ruined them.
quests.progress: Two boar hides, skinned with Agna's knife from the wild boars around her racks. Loot the body first, then skin it.
quests.complete: Agna holds each hide to the light and grunts. “One hole. I have seen worse. I have done worse.” She takes the knife back and wipes it on her apron. “Skinning is yours. Knives are mine, and I sell them.”
quests.turnInLog: Agna teaches you Skinning and takes back her knife. She sells skinning knives.

objectives.label: Boar hides skinned from wild boars

quests.name: Bitter Roots
quests.summary: Morrow Finch lends you an herb knife. Cut three ditchbell from the marked patches along the Briarwood path and bring them to Morrow at Mourning Hollow.
quests.offer: Everyone wants a draught. Nobody wants to kneel in a ditch for one. Take my herb knife: cut, do not pull, or the root dies and next year there is nothing. Ditchbell grows along the Briarwood path, blue and sulking. Three sprigs, and the knife back.
quests.progress: Three ditchbell from the Briarwood path, cut with Morrow's knife. Morrow waits at Mourning Hollow.
quests.complete: Morrow sniffs each sprig and sets them in a row. “Cut clean. Good. A plant you cut properly forgives you.” The knife goes back on its hook. “Herbalism is yours. Come back when you can tell woundwort from a weed by smell alone, and I will teach you to brew.”
quests.turnInLog: Morrow teaches you Herbalism and takes back the herb knife.

quests.name: A Calling
quests.summary: Mayor Alder says Captain Rowan wants to see you. Find Rowan at the watch barracks by the square.
quests.offer: You have done more for Thornford this week than the watch has all season. Do not tell them I said so; they are touchy. Rowan has asked after you. He trains the watch's fighters, and he says you hold a blade like someone who means it, which he also says about the cook.
quests.progress: Captain Rowan is waiting for you at the watch barracks by the square.
quests.complete: Rowan looks you up and down. “Alder says you can fight. Alder thinks a bread knife is a weapon. Let us find out.”

quests.name: A Calling
quests.summary: Mayor Alder says Mira Vale wants to see you. Find Mira Vale at the inn's back room.
quests.offer: You have done more for Thornford this week than the watch has all season. Do not tell them I said so; they are touchy. There is a woman called Mira Vale who drinks in the corner of the Lantern Inn and never seems to pay. She asked about you. I would rather she asked about you than about me.
quests.progress: Mira Vale is waiting for you at the inn's back room.
quests.complete: Mira does not look up from her cup. “You walked in the front door. Everyone saw you. We will fix that.”

quests.name: A Calling
quests.summary: Mayor Alder says Scout Fen wants to see you. Find Fen at Briarwood Camp.
quests.offer: You have done more for Thornford this week than the watch has all season. Do not tell them I said so; they are touchy. Scout Fen came down from Briarwood to ask if the new arrival can shoot. I said you could certainly carry a bow. He wants to see for himself.
quests.progress: Scout Fen is waiting for you at Briarwood Camp.
quests.complete: Fen nods at your bow. “You carry it like a walking stick. Good. Means you have not learned anything wrong yet.”

quests.name: A Calling
quests.summary: Mayor Alder says Morrow Finch wants to see you. Find Morrow Finch at Mourning Hollow.
quests.offer: You have done more for Thornford this week than the watch has all season. Do not tell them I said so; they are touchy. Morrow Finch sent word from Mourning Hollow. Morrow does not send word. Morrow sends bottles with labels I prefer not to read. Go and see what they want.
quests.progress: Morrow Finch is waiting for you at Mourning Hollow.
quests.complete: Morrow corks a bottle that was, for a moment, whispering. “Ah. You came. Most people stop at the gate and remember an errand.”

quests.name: A Calling
quests.summary: Mayor Alder says Sister Lyra wants to see you. Find Lyra at the shrine path south of the square.
quests.offer: You have done more for Thornford this week than the watch has all season. Do not tell them I said so; they are touchy. Sister Lyra has been asking for you. She says the light has opinions about you. I said the light can queue like everyone else, but here we are.
quests.progress: Sister Lyra is waiting for you at the shrine path south of the square.
quests.complete: Lyra takes your hands and turns them palm up as if reading them. “They are not soft. Good. The light is not for the soft.”

quests.name: The Wide Swing
quests.summary: Captain Rowan asks you to practise Cleave. Use it on the young boars in Holt Meadow three times, then report back.
quests.offer: One enemy at a time is a luxury. Out there they come in threes and fours and none of them wait their turn. Plant your feet, turn from the hips, and take the whole front rank with you. That is Cleave. Go and practise on Heda's young boars; they come in herds and nobody will miss them. Three good swings.
quests.progress: Cleave the young boars in Holt Meadow three times. Target one; the swing takes whatever stands beside it.
quests.complete: Rowan watches you roll your shoulder. “Sore? Good. That is where the swing lives now.” He almost smiles. “The watch could use more like you. The watch could use more of anything.”

quests.name: Unseen
quests.summary: Mira Vale asks you to practise Shadow. Slip into it among the risen dead at the Nameless Yard, then look at the Bell Crypt's door without being caught.
quests.offer: Shadow is not magic, whatever the songs say. It is knowing where people are not looking. The dead are worse at it than the living, which makes them good practice. Go to the Nameless Yard south of Mourning Hollow, step into Shadow among them, and walk up to the Bell Crypt's door. Tell me what is carved on it.
quests.progress: Use Shadow at the Nameless Yard among the risen dead, then look over the Bell Crypt's door.
quests.complete: “A bell with a crack through it,” Mira repeats, and taps the table twice. “You looked. You came back. Two things most people only manage one of.”

objectives.label: Slip into Shadow at the Nameless Yard
Look over the Bell Crypt's door

quests.name: Tar and Patience
quests.summary: Scout Fen asks you to practise Tar Trap. Lay two traps in Wolf Hollow and thin out three of the wolves that run into them.
quests.offer: A wolf runs faster than you and it knows it. So you do not chase. You put a trap where it is going and let it come to you. Tar Trap: set it at your feet, step back, and let them come. Lay two in Wolf Hollow, then put three wolves down while they are stuck. You have seen me do it. Well, you have heard me talk about it.
quests.progress: Lay two Tar Traps in Wolf Hollow and kill three wolves.
quests.complete: Fen picks tar off your boot and sniffs it. “You stood in your own trap. Everyone does, once.” He hands the boot back. “The wolves did not. That is the bit that counts.”

objectives.label: Lay Tar Traps in Wolf Hollow

quests.name: What Grows on Graves
quests.summary: Use Rot three times and Soul Ward once in Nameless Yard, then return to Morrow.
quests.offer: “Apply Rot three times in the yard. Let it build Corruption, then spend some on Soul Ward. Power is useful. Knowing when to stop borrowing it is a profession.”
quests.progress: Use Rot three times and Soul Ward once in Nameless Yard, then return to Morrow.
quests.complete: Morrow checks your hands. “Steady. Good. A ward is wiser than trying to explain a missing finger.” He writes Grave Bloom into your book and offers a balanced athame. “A second way to spend what you gather. Try it, then decide which tools belong on your bar.”

objectives.label: Apply Rot three times in Nameless Yard

quests.name: Mercy on the Lantern Road
quests.summary: Build Conviction and practise Light Shield twice near the fallen lantern. Return to Sister Lyra.
quests.offer: “A shield is a promise to stay long enough to help. Build Conviction with Holy Strike and your weapon, then practise Light Shield twice on the Lantern Road. Step out of danger while it recovers. You can care for people without offering every monster a free swing.”
quests.progress: Build Conviction and practise Light Shield twice near the fallen lantern. Return to Sister Lyra.
quests.complete: Lyra checks the nicks on your shield. “You stayed long enough to help and moved before you needed rescuing. Good. Conviction is useful when it protects somebody.” She offers a balanced watch sword. “Equip this before the next patrol. Protection is a craft, and crafts deserve sound tools.”
quests.turnInLog: Watchman Dunn kept muttering about lantern-bearers who did not carry lanterns. You remember it.

objectives.label: Practise Light Shield on the Lantern Road

quests.name: An Honest Day’s Work
quests.summary: Help Heda protect her orchard. Clear three young boars, inspect the broken fence, then return to her farm gate.
quests.offer: “Those are wild boars in the orchard, before you ask. My pigs have names and better manners. Thin out three young boars, then look at the broken fence. Leave the big ones alone for now. You will find me here when the job is done.”
quests.progress: Help Heda protect her orchard. Clear three young boars, inspect the broken fence, then return to her farm gate.
quests.complete: Heda counts the pigs twice. “Three. Excellent. Last week I was down to two pigs and a very convincing argument.” She presses your pay into your hand. “The fence needs timber. Osric is waiting for the watch to bring it. Ask Rowan where his patrol went.”

quests.name: The Names They Left Behind
quests.summary: Read the altered headstones at Nameless Yard and lay three gravewalkers to rest. Bring the evidence to Mayor Alder.
quests.offer: Morrow opens the parish book. “Read the memorial stones in Nameless Yard and lay three of the wandering watchmen to rest. Remember whose names have been taken. Tell Mayor Alder in Thornford what you find. He signed the grain contract. It is time he saw who is paying for it.”
quests.progress: Take Mourning Road east of Old Watch. The yard lies south of Morrow’s apothecary. Copy the altered stones and put three gravewalkers down.
quests.complete: Alder lays your account beside the contract. “My mother’s family. Elsie’s father. Paid debts copied onto dead names.” He uncaps his ink. “My signature let the clerk in. Mine will go on the inquiry. First, ask Benn the gravekeeper for permission to copy the family stones. Morrow needs an independent record.”

quests.name: What the Bell Remembers
quests.summary: Find Bell Crypt beyond Nameless Yard and defeat the Keeper of the Lost Names. Return to Alder with the family seals.
quests.offer: The collector bound the stolen names to our family seals. The crypt keeper carries them. Find Bell Crypt beyond the yard and end his watch. I will put the real names back where they belong. There will be an inquiry afterwards. I intend to attend it, which is an unfashionable position for a mayor.
quests.progress: Bell Crypt is beyond the southern graves. Defeat the Keeper of the Lost Names and return here. Lyra will help the families once the seals are safe.
quests.complete: Alder presses the recovered seals into the book. The scratched names darken into legible ink. “No more names leave this roll. Tonight we read them aloud.” He prepares two letters. “When you are ready, choose a road. Merrit at Lantern Crossing needs reliable hands east of Thornford. Nessa at Mossreed Landing keeps the ferry community northwest along Ferry Ridge. Both have seen Rook’s collectors. Either will know where this account belongs.”

objectives.label: Keeper of the Lost Names defeated

quests.name: Supper at the Lantern
quests.summary: Catch three Gloomwater perch at Willow Pond or Miller's Pool and bring them to Elsie inside the Lantern Inn.
quests.offer: Tobin teaches Fishing by Willow Pond. If you have a rod, three perch would make a fine supper. You can fish the mill pool too. Take your time. Some work is better done sitting quietly.
quests.progress: Bring three Gloomwater perch to Elsie inside the Lantern Inn. Tobin sells rods and teaches Fishing at Willow Pond; Miller’s Pool works too.
quests.complete: “Three perch! Supper is saved.” Elsie sets a pan by the hearth. “Tobin says patience is its own reward. He has never tried paying a flour merchant with it.”

quests.name: The House That Kept a Light
quests.summary: Visit Widow's Mirror beside Mourning Hollow, then return to Morrow at the apothecary. This local tale is independent of the watch story.
quests.offer: The widow kept a light beside that pool after her son failed to return. Folk call it haunted. I call it a place to remember someone. Go and look, if you can spare a moment from hunting monsters.
quests.progress: Visit Widow’s Mirror, southeast of the apothecary. Return to Morrow; neither Fishing nor the watch investigation is required.
quests.complete: Morrow sets a cup beside the window. 'She knew he was gone. The light was for anyone else who might still find their way home.'

quests.name: Three Paces Over the Line
quests.summary: Heda and Osric disagree over the orchard boundary. Read the old boundary stone beside their plots and report to Mayor Alder.
quests.offer: Heda says Osric moved the fence. Osric says the hedge was never straight. Neither will speak to the other. Look at the old boundary stone by the orchard trail and bring me what it actually says.
quests.progress: Read the boundary stone beside the orchard timber trail, then report to Alder inside the town hall.
quests.complete: “Three paces.” Alder reaches for the parish ruler. “Osric will hear the ruling from me. Heda will hear it from him, twice, across the hedge. Neither will be charged a fee. I should like one dispute in this village to cost less than the fence.”

quests.name: One Pig Too Many
quests.summary: Briarjaw has killed two of Heda's pigs. Track the lone wolf east of Holt Meadow and return to Heda.
quests.offer: First the orchard fence, now my pigs. Two gone, and that grey wolf is bold enough to come back for a third. They call it Briarjaw. Follow its run east of the meadow and put a stop to it.
quests.progress: Briarjaw’s run is east of Heda’s pigpen. Defeat the lone wolf, then return to Heda at the farm.
quests.complete: Heda checks the pen before she takes your hand. 'Still three. You have no idea how glad I am to count the same number twice. Here, for your trouble.'

quests.name: A Word Across the Water
quests.summary: Carry Heda's request for fence reeds to Tobin at Willow Pond.
quests.offer: If you are going past Willow Pond, tell Tobin I will trade orchard apples for a bundle of his cut reeds. The pig shelter needs a new roof, and neither of us has time to leave our work.
quests.progress: Deliver Heda’s reeds-for-apples offer to Tobin at Willow Pond. Tobin is the recipient; there is no need to come back to Heda.
quests.complete: “Apples for reeds? Done. I will take them round after dusk.” Tobin smiles. “Heda counts apples like a tax collector, but hers are at least edible.”

quests.name: Lost in the Rushes
quests.summary: Find Elsie's keepsake pouch beside Miller's Pool and return it to her inside the Lantern Inn.
quests.offer: I took a walk by the mill pool before opening the inn. Somewhere near the rushes I dropped a little pouch with Mother's brass brooch inside. It is worth almost nothing to anyone else. Would you look for it?
quests.progress: The keepsake pouch lies beside the rushes on the south bank of Miller’s Pool, west of the inn. Return it to Elsie indoors.
quests.complete: Elsie opens the pouch, then closes her fingers round the brooch. 'I thought I had lost her twice. Thank you. Have something for the road.'

quests.name: A Gauge Worth Trusting
quests.summary: Compare the two stamped measures just east of Iren’s forge. Recover the gauge case and return it to Iren.
quests.offer: Someone says my axe heads are short. Someone used a gauge that thinks an inch grows with age. Compare the master stamp beside my forge with the rejected gauge south of it. Bring the gauge’s case back. If I am wrong, I will say so. Do not look so alarmed; it has happened before.
quests.progress: Compare the two stamped measures just east of Iren’s forge. Recover the gauge case and return it to Iren.
quests.complete: Iren fits the split marks together. “Slipped hinge. My work is sound. My temper could use filing.” She puts the bad gauge aside. “Thanks for checking before deciding which of us to insult.”

quests.name: The Dry Stack
quests.summary: Take the two tagged billets beside Osric’s woodlot to Iren at the Thornford smithy. Iren receives the delivery.
quests.offer: Two dry handle billets, from the tagged stack beside me, for Iren’s smithy. I spent a year seasoning them. Last week someone called them kindling. Please deliver them before I commit a small, very well-documented crime.
quests.progress: Take the two tagged billets beside Osric’s woodlot to Iren at the Thornford smithy. Iren receives the delivery.
quests.complete: “Sound grain. Dry as a sermon on parish drainage.” Iren sets the billets under cover. “Tell Osric I know the difference between his work and kindling. You can leave out the sermon bit.”

quests.name: Two Waters, One Notebook
quests.summary: Read the observation boards at Willow Pond’s northwestern reed edge and Miller’s Pool’s north bank. Report to Tobin.
quests.offer: Willow’s reeds, Miller’s open bank. Have a proper look at both and tell me where the fish shelter. You need not catch anything. An angler who can only describe the one that got away is a man with a rod, not a source.
quests.progress: Read the observation boards at Willow Pond’s northwestern reed edge and Miller’s Pool’s north bank. Report to Tobin.
quests.complete: Tobin adds your observations. “Shade in both, different water. Useful.” He closes the book. “I shall ruin it later by adding a sketch of a trout I have never actually caught.”

quests.name: The Route on the Reverse
quests.summary: Read the split-stump mark on Briarwood Loop, west of Lantern Road and the pale-boulder mark on Briarwood Camp’s eastern approach. Return to Mira inside the inn.
quests.offer: People hire me to find doors. Then they walk straight past the way home. Check the split-stump mark on Briarwood Loop, west of Lantern Road and the pale boulder near Fen’s camp. Read both faces. No theft, no ambush, no dramatic leap. I am trying a radical new teaching method called arriving alive.
quests.progress: Read the split-stump mark on Briarwood Loop, west of Lantern Road and the pale-boulder mark on Briarwood Camp’s eastern approach. Return to Mira inside the inn.
quests.complete: “Two marks, one route, a way home.” Mira nods. “You would be amazed how many professionals stop at two marks and a regrettable funeral.”

quests.name: No One Turned Away
quests.summary: Collect Elsie’s two marked bedding rolls outside the inn’s west door and bring them to Sister Lyra beside the chapel.
quests.offer: Two travellers came in soaked. The chapel has a roof; the inn has spare bedding. Elsie has set two clean rolls outside her west door for us. Bring them here. No relic hunt, I am afraid. Holiness is mostly carrying things after everyone else has gone to bed.
quests.progress: Collect Elsie’s two marked bedding rolls outside the inn’s west door and bring them to Sister Lyra beside the chapel.
quests.complete: Lyra stacks the rolls under cover. “Dry bedding, no questions about their purse. That will do more good tonight than my best argument.” She smiles. “Do not tell the bishop. He spent years teaching me the argument.”

quests.name: A Shelter, Not a Lair
quests.summary: Inspect the bootprints and borrowed-kettle note at the small shelter south of Briarwood Camp. Return to Fen.
quests.offer: Smoke by the old shelter. Someone at the inn called it bandits. Could be a family trying to keep warm. Check the tracks and the note box south of camp. Tell me what is there before anyone goes out to make a hero of himself.
quests.progress: Inspect the bootprints and borrowed-kettle note at the small shelter south of Briarwood Camp. Return to Fen.
quests.complete: “A family. Good.” Fen folds your copy. “I shall send food, not a patrol. Amazing what one can learn by reading a note before drawing a sword.”

quests.name: The Label Facing In
quests.summary: Read Morrow’s shelf list just west of the apothecary and collect both loose labels nearby. Return to Morrow.
quests.offer: The shelf list is sound. The labels have deserted. Read the list beside my door, gather the two loose tags from the sorting trays, and bring them to me. I will reattach them. My customers deserve sleep without unexpectedly waterproof feet.
quests.progress: Read Morrow’s shelf list just west of the apothecary and collect both loose labels nearby. Return to Morrow.
quests.complete: Morrow matches the tags to the list. “There. No one drinks the boot liniment.” He reaches for his pen. “I shall label the label tray next. We must not let the paperwork win.”

quests.name: The Orchard’s Small Tenants
quests.summary: Inspect the quiet bee box on the orchard’s north edge and the eastern blossom branch. Return to Heda.
quests.offer: The blossoms look healthy, but there are hardly any bees. Check the little bee box by the north fence and the flowering branch east of the pen. Boars are loud problems. This one can empty a pantry without making a sound.
quests.progress: Inspect the quiet bee box on the orchard’s north edge and the eastern blossom branch. Return to Heda.
quests.complete: Heda fetches a small board. “A roof repair. I can manage that.” She glances toward the pigpen. “The smallest tenants ask the least and pay on time. I ought to put them on the council.”

objectives.label: Check the orchard’s quiet bee box

quests.name: No Overtime for the Dead
quests.summary: Lay two Fallen Watch Sentries to rest around Old Watch, north of the lantern cart. Return to Rowan.
quests.offer: Two fallen sentries still march round Old Watch. They are saluting people who cannot see them and attacking the ones who can. Put both down. I have their families’ names. This is not a bounty on strangers.
quests.progress: Lay two Fallen Watch Sentries to rest around Old Watch, north of the lantern cart. Return to Rowan.

objectives.label: Fallen Watch Sentries laid to rest

quests.name: Quiet Hours
quests.summary: Defeat the two Hollow Watch Archers at Nameless Yard. Return to Morrow at the Mourning Hollow apothecary.
quests.offer: The two dead archers in Nameless Yard loose arrows whenever a shutter moves. I cannot ask a neighbour to collect medicine through that. Deal with them, please. I used to write “avoid strenuous activity” on prescriptions. I did not mean incoming arrows.
quests.progress: Defeat the two Hollow Watch Archers at Nameless Yard. Return to Morrow at the Mourning Hollow apothecary.
quests.complete: “Both of them? Good.” Morrow moves the delivery basket beside the door. “The living can collect their medicine. The dead may lodge a complaint in person during office hours.”

quests.name: Reasonable Use
quests.summary: Read the allocation board just south of Willow Lane, west of Willow Pond. Set the Orchard, Mill and Pond handles, then test the flow. Report to Tobin.
quests.offer: Osric wants more water, the mill wants all of it, and my pond would like to remain a pond. The regulator is just south of Willow Lane, west of my landing. Read its allocation board. Turn the three handles to the agreed shares, then test the float. No wet feet, no injured parties, and ideally no committee.
quests.progress: Read the allocation board just south of Willow Lane, west of Willow Pond. Set the Orchard, Mill and Pond handles, then test the flow. Report to Tobin.
quests.complete: Tobin checks the float mark. “The agreed shares. Remarkable. We have settled a water dispute using the agreement.” He pockets his notebook. “I shall tell the council slowly.”

quests.name: The Bell’s Last Word
quests.summary: After returning the burial seals, read the memorial verse at Nameless Yard’s western edge. Ring the four small bells in its order, then return to Lyra.
quests.offer: The seals are back. The families want a farewell in their own words. At the western edge of Nameless Yard are four small bells and an old verse. Ring a life in the order the verse remembers it. No haste. The collector had plenty of instructions; he need not have the last word.
quests.progress: After returning the burial seals, read the memorial verse at Nameless Yard’s western edge. Ring the four small bells in its order, then return to Lyra.
quests.complete: Lyra closes the memorial book. “A home. A day’s work. The way back. Rest. Enough for a life, if we let it be.” She folds the paper into her sleeve. “There will be washing up after the gathering. I have promised Alder he can be useful without signing anything.”

quests.name: A Crossing Worth Keeping
quests.summary: Clear the cutpurses by the marked cartway northwest of the crossing. Read their notice and report to Ada at her shed.
quests.offer: “That account from Thornford matches our grain tallies. First we keep people moving. Four cutpurses have taken the cartway and called it an office. Clear them out, read their notice, then find Ada at the cart shed. She knows which bits of this bridge are actually broken.”
quests.progress: Clear the cutpurses by the marked cartway northwest of the crossing. Read their notice and report to Ada at her shed.
quests.complete: Ada wipes her hands. “Excellent. Now the armed accountants have left, we can attend to the timber. It was beginning to feel neglected.”

quests.progress: Recover the existing packet at the cartway and check the bridge brace, then return to Merrit.
quests.complete: “Two copies. One here and one with you. If somebody loses ours, it will have to be on purpose.” Merrit gives you Sella’s directions. “She is west along the lamplit ridge. Tell her these people have already paid.”

quests.name: Beren’s Borrowed Shovel

quests.progress: Recover the existing packet beside the ferry worksite, speak to Hale, then return to Nessa.
quests.complete: “One copy stays dry here. The other goes with you.” Nessa ties the packet shut. “Follow the ridge lamps east. Give Sella my regards, and tell her I would like my boatmen home before supper.”

quests.name: Hawthorn's Blind
quests.summary: Scout Fen's teacher, the fletcher Hawthorn Ide, went into Wolf Hollow and did not come out. Find her old hunting blind east of the hollow.
quests.offer: Before I was a scout I was Hawthorn Ide's apprentice. She made arrows, and she never lost one. Not one, in thirty years. Three winters ago she went into the hollow after a wolf and I found her bow, and nothing else. Her blind is still out there, east of the hollow. I have not had the stomach to look. Will you?
quests.progress: Her blind is east of Wolf Hollow, under the leaning pine. Tell me what is left of it.
quests.complete: Fen turns the cut shafts over in his hands. “She was making new ones. Sinew bindings, grey fletching. She never left a job half done. So neither shall I.”

quests.name: Sinew and Shafts
quests.summary: Bring Scout Fen wolf sinew for the bindings, and recover the arrow bundle Hawthorn hid by the hollow.
quests.offer: Her quiver was a strange thing. She sewed it herself, and the arrows came home to it. She called it a gathering quiver. I mean to make it again. I need sinew from the Briarwood wolves, five lengths, and her last bundle of shafts. She cached them in a crate by the hollow. She cached everything.
quests.progress: Five lengths of wolf sinew, and Hawthorn's arrow cache by the hollow.
quests.complete: “Good sinew. Better shafts.” Fen lays them out on a cloth. “There is one thing still missing. Her pattern was sewn into the old quiver's lining. And the old quiver is wherever she is.”

quests.name: The Gathering Quiver
quests.summary: Find where Hawthorn Ide fell in Wolf Hollow, thin the wolves that still den there, and bring her quiver lining back to Scout Fen.
quests.offer: I know where she is. I always have. There is a stone at the south end of the hollow and the wolves den beside it. Thin them out and look at the stone. Bring me what you find. Then you can have the quiver. I cannot draw a bow these days anyway.
quests.progress: The stone at the south end of Wolf Hollow. Four wolves, then look.
quests.complete: Fen is quiet a long while over the scrap of lining. Then he sews. When he is done he hands you the quiver. “She would want it shooting, not on a peg. One in four comes home to it. Do not ask me how. She never told me either.”
quests.turnInLog: You hand Fen the scrap of quiver lining, and the closed eye cut into the stone weighs on you.

objectives.label: Look at the stone where Hawthorn fell

quests.complete: Morrow sets the rubbings beside the ledger. “Three people, three settled accounts, and three demands for another winter’s service. Benn was right to keep his own book. The seals in the crypt are holding this forgery together.”

quests.name: The Supper Round
quests.summary: Visit Della at the shuttered cottage and Benn at Nameless Yard. Return to Morrow when both have been checked on.

quests.name: A Proper Hem

quests.progress: Recover the sewing tin beside the old well east of Della’s cottage, then return it to her.
quests.complete: Della draws out the blue thread. “That will do. He says he does not feel the cold. Men will say anything to avoid standing still for a fitting.”

quests.summary: Gather three waxed wicks beside the landing stores, then speak to Hale on the southern bank path.
quests.offer: “Three wicks from the dry boxes. Take them to Hale by the bank lamps. He frightens visitors, but he has never once forgotten to light the way home. That is better than half the living boatmen manage.”
quests.progress: Gather three waxed wicks beside the landing stores, then speak to Hale on the southern bank path.
quests.complete: Hale takes the wicks with careful, bare fingers. “Thank you. A man should keep doing something useful while everyone decides what he is.” He points to the depth marker. “Nessa will want that sluice checked next.”

quests.name: A Little Give and Take

quests.offer: “The bank needs a trickle. The ferry needs the full channel. Nessa painted it on the marker after Jory’s third unsuccessful experiment. Turn the two handles, test the flow and tell her how it stands. Nothing will explode. This is plumbing.”
quests.progress: Read the red depth marker. At the nearby sluice, set Bank to Trickle and Ferry to Full, then test the flow.
quests.complete: Nessa checks the float. “Good. A straightforward answer to a straightforward question. I am beginning to miss those.” She lays out a passenger list with Hale’s name crossed through twice.
